anchored_lane_cost.note: no laws resolve on this lane, so it is ~3.5x cheaper per draw than shallow

yield_measured.interpretation: a real negative for this lane on fa7_0. With 0 events in 2048 draws the one-sided 95% upper bound on its rate is about 1 per 683 draws, so it is not ruled out and it is certainly not demonstrated. The expansion's expected yield should be read off the SHALLOW lane alone

expansion_sizing_rationale.caveat: this expectation extrapolates a rate estimated from ONE eligible endpoint in 1440 draws. It is a sizing argument, not a measurement of the event, and the anchored lane's rate is not separately established
expansion_sizing_rationale.revision: the anchored lane's contribution is now measured at 0 in 2048 draws, so the sizing rests on the shallow lane alone: 6720 shallow draws per event against a rate of about 1 per 1920 measured draws gives roughly 3.5 expected eligible endpoints, i.e. P(at least one) near 0.97. A round that still exhausts after that full ladder is a bounded, documented exhaustion rather than the coin flip the unexpanded loop would have been

why_the_cell_was_blank.mechanism: select_batch returns empty exactly when candidates is empty, so the shipped loop's `if not selected` branch IS the cell's terminal condition; one empty round ended the cell with 247 calls unspent

zero_support_fallback_funnel.verdict: the fallback stage alone does NOT rescue fa7_0 on the round-one parent. It is retained because it is bounded, cheap, structurally different, and runs on the CURRENT parent, which changes every round -- but no claim rests on it for this cell
